name: Rauma
title: Ship Thickness Gauging in Rauma: Dry Dock and Cargo Port
description: UTM in Rauma for forest-product carriers, container feeders and ferries docking at the shipyard: hull, hold, ballast tank and piping thickness gauging.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement for Ships at the Port of Rauma and Its Shipyard
intro: Rauma pairs a leading Finnish export harbour for paper, pulp and containers with a shipyard whose large dry dock takes ferries, icebreakers and government vessels for repair as well as newbuilding. That mix produces two kinds of gauging work: measurement on cargo ships during their stay alongside, and full steel surveys while a ship sits in the dock. For each Rauma job, Atlantis flies its technicians in from India, and they stay aboard for as long as the call or the docking allows.

highlights.h: Gauging in a large Baltic dry dock
highlights.p: Rauma Marine Constructions docks ferries, icebreakers and state vessels for maintenance and overhaul in a dry dock it ranks among the largest in the Baltic. Readings taken in the first days of a stay feed directly into the steel list that the yard and surveyor settle.

highlights.h: Paper and pulp carriers on long calls
highlights.p: Sto-ro and lo-lo ships loading paper reels and pulp bales stay alongside long enough for tank-top, hold-frame and hatch-cover readings, as long as the team keeps ahead of the stevedores and dries every measured patch before cargo goes in.

highlights.h: Bothnian Sea winters on the ice belt
highlights.p: Ships serving Rauma through the winter spend weeks at a time in Bothnian Sea ice. Measuring the bow and ice belt in autumn and again at the spring docking shows an owner how fast the remaining margin is being consumed.

port.h: Rauma: forest-industry harbour and docking yard
p: Rauma lies on the Bothnian Sea coast of south-west Finland, and its harbour is reached through a fairway past low skerries rather than the long island passage that ships bound for Turku must make. The port grew with the forest industry around it: pulp and paper mills in and near the town ship their output in sto-ro and lo-lo vessels to customers across north-west Europe, and the container terminal ties Rauma to the North Sea hubs by feeder. Dry bulk, liquid chemicals, general cargo and heavy project lifts for regional industry make up the rest. Because much of the liner traffic runs on fixed weekly loops, the same ships come back again and again, which makes it practical to build a thickness record across several calls instead of one.

The other half of Rauma's maritime life is the shipyard on the town's waterfront. Rauma Marine Constructions builds ferries and naval vessels there, and it also takes ships already in service into its dry dock for maintenance, repair, conversion and overhaul; Baltic ro-pax ferries, state icebreakers and government patrol and pollution-response ships have all docked at Rauma in recent years. For an owner, this means a ship trading on the Finnish coast can be docked without a long positioning voyage, and the dock period is when the full renewal-survey programme, the bottom plating and the sea chests can be measured with staging and lighting supplied by the yard. Newbuilding inspection is a matter for the builder, the owner's site team and the classification society, so our work at the yard concerns ships in service.

Winter shapes almost everything here. In a normal year ice forms along the Bothnian Sea coast, and the Finnish winter traffic restrictions set the minimum ice class and size a ship needs before icebreakers will assist it into port. Most regular liner tonnage on Rauma routes is built to a Finnish-Swedish ice class for that reason, and its ice belt takes a beating every season. Dockings tend to be booked outside the deep winter and away from the summer ferry peak, which pushes repair-yard gauging towards spring and autumn. In the harbour, forest-product ships commonly stay a day or more, while tankers at the chemical berths keep to shorter visits. Ships that arrive before their berth is free can anchor off the port when ice and weather allow, and are reached by launch.

facilities.h: Where a ship can be gauged in Rauma
p: The dry dock at the shipyard is where the largest scopes are done. Once the ship is dry and the yard has cleaned and ventilated the first tanks, we begin with the areas most likely to need renewal, usually the ballast tanks, the double bottom under the engine room and the ice belt, so that the class surveyor and the yard can settle quantities while steel can still be ordered without delaying undocking. Staging, lifts and lighting come from the yard under the owner's docking contract, and the readings go to the superintendent each evening, laid out so the yard's planners can size the renewal straight from them.

In the commercial harbour, gauging fits around the cargo. Forest-product berths give access to empty holds and tween decks before loading starts and to deck structure throughout the stay; the container terminal suits short deck and scrubber-piping jobs on feeders within one working day; and tankers at the liquid berths can have deck, piping and certified-safe void spaces measured under the ship's own permit system. A ship that loads at Rauma and is heading for a yard elsewhere can have its pre-docking steel estimate prepared during the call, and that estimate sometimes persuades the owner to dock at Rauma itself.
list: Rauma Marine Constructions dry dock — renewal-survey gauging of bottom and side shell, sea chests and tanks on ferries, icebreakers and government ships in for repair
Shipyard quays — afloat repair periods, where piping, deck and tank readings confirm which sections the yard should renew
Forest-product berths — holds, tween decks and hatch covers on sto-ro and lo-lo ships, measured before loading begins
Container terminal — deck plating and scrubber wash-water and overboard lines on feeders, completed within one call
Liquid bulk berths — deck plating, cargo and ballast piping and safe voids on chemical and product tankers
Anchorage off the port — ships waiting for a berth or for ice assistance, boarded by launch arranged through the agent

context.h: Port state control, ice rules and the Bothnian Sea trade
p: Port state control in Rauma is carried out by Traficom, the Finnish Transport and Communications Agency, within the Paris MoU, and boardings follow each ship's risk profile, so older bulk carriers and general cargo ships with past structural deficiencies are more likely to be inspected. The Bothnian Sea lies within the Baltic NOx emission control area for ships built from 2021 onwards. Voyages between Rauma and other EU ports have counted under the EU ETS since 2024 and under FuelEU Maritime since 2025, and the EU Ship Recycling Regulation obliges ships of 500 gross tonnage and upwards calling at EU ports to carry an Inventory of Hazardous Materials, which owners often bring up to date in the same docking that covers the renewal survey.

Ice class is the commercial lever in this trade. The Finnish-Swedish Ice Class Rules grade ships from IA Super downwards, and in a severe winter the restrictions for Bothnian Sea ports can climb high enough to shut out lower-class tonnage altogether. Charterers moving paper and pulp on year-round contracts therefore want ships whose ice class is secure, and that depends on ice-belt plating and frames keeping enough of their abrasion allowance. Thickness data from the bow, the forward shoulders and the midship ice belt gives an owner the evidence to keep a ship on such a contract, or the warning that renewal must come before the next season begins.

jobs.h: Gauging work we see at Rauma
jobs.p: Rauma work divides between the dock and the quay. Dockings bring the large programmes: renewal surveys on ferries and icebreakers, steel estimates checked in the dock bottom, and piping surveys during repair periods. Cargo calls bring targeted scopes that can be finished while the ship loads, often ordered because a docking is approaching and the owner wants measured quantities before choosing a yard. Winter adds a third strand, as owners on year-round charters check ice-belt structure before the restrictions tighten. Whatever the job, the scope is written against the ship's survey status and the access the call will genuinely give, and the order of work is settled with the chief officer when the team boards.
list: Renewal-survey gauging on a Baltic ro-pax in the Rauma dry dock, with ballast tanks, voids and bottom plating measured in the first days of the stay
Ice-belt and bow plating readings on an ice-class sto-ro ship at a forest-product berth before the winter restrictions take effect
Hold frames, tank tops and hatch-cover undersides on a lo-lo ship loading pulp, measured ahead of the stevedores
Scrubber wash-water and overboard piping on a container feeder during its weekly call, with the system shut down for the readings
Sea-water, fire-main and ballast piping surveys on a government vessel at the shipyard quay during an afloat repair period
Pre-purchase gauging of a chemical tanker at the liquid berths, limited to deck, piping and gas-free spaces

logistics: Helsinki-Vantaa is the usual international gateway, and the team continues by road to the west coast; Turku Airport can shorten the journey on some itineraries. Shipyard access is arranged by the yard under the owner's docking contract, while harbour berths need ISPS passes that the ship's agent requests in advance, along with a launch if the ship is at anchor. Technicians travelling from India hold a Schengen visa for Finland, so we lock in dates once the docking slot or call is confirmed and leave room for consular processing.

faqs.q: Can you gauge our ferry while it is docked at Rauma Marine Constructions?
faqs.a: Yes, when the owner engages us and the yard accepts the team under its site safety rules. We follow the yard's programme, start in the spaces it has cleaned and ventilated first, and hand over readings every day so renewal areas can be marked and steel ordered early. If the ferry was partly gauged on its route beforehand, the dock period is used to finish the bottom, the sea chests and any tanks that could not be opened in service.

faqs.q: Is it worth gauging a cargo ship at Rauma before deciding where to dock it?
faqs.a: Often it is. Measured quantities for ballast tanks, holds and deck let an owner compare yard offers on the same steel figures instead of allowances, and they reduce the risk of the scope growing once the ship is dry. Because Rauma has a large dry dock of its own, an estimate taken during a cargo call here can also lead straight into a docking at the same port.

faqs.q: How do Bothnian Sea ice conditions affect a winter job at Rauma?
faqs.a: Inside the ship, very little: tanks, holds and piping are measured as at any time of year, using couplant suited to cold spaces. The ice affects timing and external work. Icebreaker assistance can shift a ship's arrival, launches to the anchorage may stop in heavy ice, and shell readings from outside are best left for the dock. In the ice season we keep the team's schedule flexible by a day.

faqs.q: Can holds be measured on a forest-product ship without delaying loading?
faqs.a: Yes, provided the holds are empty before loading begins and the work runs ahead of the stevedores. We start in the hold that will be loaded last, concentrate on the tank top, frames and hatch-cover undersides, and remove couplant from every measured spot because paper and pulp stain easily. Anything that cannot be reached before loading is recorded and picked up on a later call.

faqs.q: Do you test crack-prone details as well as thickness at the yard?
faqs.a: Magnetic particle and dye penetrant testing can be added where the superintendent or surveyor suspects cracking, for example at hatch-coaming brackets, ice-belt frame connections or ramp hinges on ferries. The extent is agreed before the docking so the yard can prepare the surfaces, and the findings are reported together with the thickness readings so the repair list is complete in one document.
